Let me analyze this conflict.

The register says applicant is "Goldcard Smart Group Co., Ltd"
The document (certificate itself) says applicant/manufacturer is "Goldcard Water Technology Co., Ltd."

These are two different company names. Are they the same entity? "Goldcard Smart Group Co., Ltd" vs "Goldcard Water Technology Co., Ltd." These appear to be genuinely different company names — Smart Group vs Water Technology. Goldcard Smart Group is a Chinese company (group parent), and Goldcard Water Technology could be a subsidiary. But per the rules: "Genuinely different company or person names = different-entity (best_value = the document's, since the certificate is the legal instrument)."

"Smart Group" vs "Water Technology" — these aren't spelling drift or suffix drift. They're substantively different names. The rules say genuinely different company names = different-entity, with the document's value because the certificate is the legal instrument.

Could one argue they're the same entity (parent vs subsidiary)? The rule framework is about the fused record: same-entity means the values refer to the same entity with cosmetic differences. Here the names differ substantively. Without evidence they're aliases, this is different-entity, and best_value should be the document's value since the certificate is the legal instrument.

Also note the document has both an embedded comment "applicant: Goldcard Smart Group Co., Ltd" (matching the register — likely extracted metadata) and the body text "Applicant and Manufacturer Goldcard Water Technology Co., Ltd." So the certificate body itself (the legal text) says Goldcard Water Technology Co., Ltd. That reinforces taking the document's value.

Verdict: different-entity, best_value "Goldcard Water Technology Co., Ltd."
